mini_agent 2.0.0 turns the small agent from AgentForge Tutorial 1 into a command-line tool
that installs with one command on macOS, Linux and Windows. See Install in the README.

What is new

- One-command install. `mini_agent setup` chooses a provider and stores your key;
  `mini_agent doctor` shows what is set up and what is missing.
- Many providers behind one interface: OpenRouter, DeepSeek, Anthropic Claude, OpenAI,
  Google Gemini, Alibaba Qwen, any OpenAI-compatible server, and a local Ollama server.
- Your own tools: write a Python function, add `@tool`, and give it to the agent.
- On the command line the agent asks before shell commands, Python code and file writes,
  and its file tools stay inside the folder it works in.
- Long tasks: the agent keeps your messages and a handoff note in `.mini_agent/` in that
  folder, and shortens old steps when the model's context fills up. `mini_agent -c`
  continues a task that stopped, crashed or was interrupted, in the folder it ran in,
  without running a cut-off tool call twice.
- Rate limits, server errors and timeouts are retried; a wrong key stops at once and says
  what to check.
- The exit status tells scripts how a task ended: 0 the agent finished, 1 it stopped
  before the end, 2 a usage or set-up error, 3 a risky call needs approval, 130 interrupted.

Tutorial notebooks

- The Tutorial 1 and Tutorial 2 Colab notebooks install this release. Offline mode replays
  the same recorded runs as before. Copies of the notebooks saved before this release keep
  installing version 1.2.2.

Worth knowing when you upgrade

- Session logs are now kept in `~/.mini_agent/sessions`, with your settings and notes.
- In Python, `Agent` runs every tool without asking unless you pass `approve="ask"`.
